newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast cocoa factory deal all but complete.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast cocoa factory deal all but complete.

text.p: Ivorian exporter SICC and U.S. commodities giant Cargill are close to agreement on building a new cocoa processing factory in Ivory Coast with an annual capacity of 65,000 tonnes, industry sources said.
"We expect a deal to be signed today," one source told Reuters. Another said the signing of the deal on construction could place before the weekend.
Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauze said the deal was in line with Ivory Coast's stated policy of processing 50 percent of its annual cocoa production locally by the year 2000.

"It is a project which enters into our policy of adding value to our production. That is, processing the maximum amount of beans into semi-finished and finished products," Gauze told Reuters on the sidelines of a cocoa sector reform conference on Wednesday.

"Our objective will be reached. Barely three years remain and when a balance is drawn up of proposals for industrial plants we can see a trend consolidating which will allow us to reach the objective." Gauze added.
